newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. sailor indicted in Japan for attempted rape.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sailor indicted in Japan for attempted rape.

text.p: A sailor stationed at a U.S. base in northern Japan has been indicted for attempted rape and assault causing injury on a Japanese woman last month, prosecutors said on Tuesday.
Japanese authorities in Hachinohe in rural Aomori prefecture on Monday indicted Chief Petty Officer Raymond Cunningham, the Aomori District Prosecutors office said.

Cunningham, 39, is accused of assaulting a Hachinohe woman in a rape attempt on March 20. Prosecutors allege he struck the women in the face and knocked her down, causing injuries which required two weeks treatment in hospital.

Cunningham, who is stationed at the U.S. air base at Misawa, 560 km (350 miles) north of Tokyo, was transferred to the custody of Japanese police after being held at a U.S. military facility until the indictment on Monday under the terms of a bilateral status of forces agreement.
The date of his trial has not been set, prosecutors said.
The indictment came a week after U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen addressed U.S. forces stationed outside Tokyo and urged them to behave as their country's ambassadors in Japan.

Crimes by members of the 47,000 U.S. military personnel in Japan have come under close scrutiny since the September 1995 rape of a schoolgirl in Okinawa by three U.S. servicemen stationed on the southern Japanese island.
The servicemen, two Marines and a sailor, received prison sentences of 6-1/2 to seven years for the attack, which triggered widespread protests against the heavy U.S. military presence on Okinawa.
